title: No test for scan() with CRLF line endings
description:
The README and lib.rs doc claim CRLF line endings are handled correctly. The decode.rs tests include a crlf_line_endings test. However, there is no corresponding test in scan.rs or the integration tests that exercises scan() with CRLF input.

CRLF handling in scan.rs (lines 21-22) strips the trailing CR from each line before processing. This code path is untested.

A regression in the CRLF stripping in scan.rs (e.g. an off-by-one in the line boundary calculation that leaves a \r in the trimmed line) could silently cause:
- begin-line detection failure (is_begin_line would not match 'begin\r ...')
- end-line detection failure (is_end_line would not match 'end\r')
- decode_line treating '\r' as an extra encoded character

Missing test: scan() on a full CRLF-encoded UU block should yield the same result as on a LF-encoded block.

Fix: Add a test in scan.rs::tests that exercises scan_impl() on a CRLF input (e.g. the HELLO_BLOCK with all \n replaced by \r\n) and asserts the same result as for the LF version.
